text:
maya: heads up — support escalated: customer can't reconcile invoice lines back to individual requests for a security audit. they want a clear forensics path
eli: are we propagating any request id through billing events today?
maya: not reliably. the edge proxy sets X-Req-Id in many cases but the metering producer drops it before the ingest topic.
donna: we have request ids in debug logs, and in traces, but billing_event schema purposely kept small to save storage. thats biting us now.
samir: suggestion: add billing_request_id (optional string) to the canonical billing event envelope. consumers can join on it when present. downsides: cardinality and slightly bigger events.
maya: customer needs the ability to supply a list of their request ids and get invoice detail back. optional field sounds right.
eli: edge case: multiple ids per logical operation (client_id, edge_req_id, internal_retry_id). we need a single canonical id and clear mapping rules.
donna: propose that the first trusted ingress (edge/proxy) mints billing_request_id and maps any client-provided id to it. sidecars copy X-Billing-Req into the metering event.
samir: example envoy filter we can use in proxy:
```
# envoy ext_authz or header manipulation
add_request_header: "x-billing-req
%REQ(X-Req-Id)%"
```
metering-sidecar can read x-billing-req and set event.billing_request_id

maya: can we also capture a tiny origin tag like billing_request_origin="edge-host1" so we can debug where it was set? keep it short to avoid high cardinality.
eli: prefer a single origin string rather than an array to avoid explosion. billing_request_origin is fine.
donna: compatibility concern: if we change the Avro schema, will older aggregators fail? we rely on forward-compatible schema evolution but need to verify all consumers ignore unknown fields.
samir: rollout plan: 1) add optional fields in schema (billing_request_id, billing_request_origin), 2) deploy sidecar change in canary namespace, 3) enable producer to emit fields, 4) add consumer acceptance tests and exporters, 5) console filter + CSV export, 6) privacy/legal review.
maya: console UX ask from product: invoice preview should support filtering by billing_request_id and allow CSV export of matching invoice-event lines for audits.
legal: @maya important: if the client supplies an identifier that could be PII, we need to treat client_provided_id differently and run privacy review. we may need explicit consent before persisting raw client ids. also track the timestamp when mapping occurred.
maya: acknowledged. default persist only billing_request_id; persist client_provided_id only if consented and mark it with redaction metadata.
samir: feature flags for rollout: METADATA_BILLING_REQ=on in canary, off elsewhere. sampling option: start at 1% of traffic to measure storage impact, then ramp.
donna: metrics to monitor: event size p50/p95, producer throughput, downstream index card., invoice_preview latency. alert if event p95 size increases > 15% or index cardinality spikes.
maya: quick SQL support used to illustrate join for now:
```
SELECT b.invoice_id, e.request_id, e.tokens
FROM billing_events b
LEFT JOIN raw_metering_events e ON e.billing_request_id = b.billing_request_id
WHERE b.tenant_id = 'acme' AND b.invoice_date = '2026-02-01';
```
eli: i'll draft the schema spec and sample event and post back.
deploy-bot: starting canary deploy for metering-sidecar v2.1 -> ns=canary (ETA ~10m) :rocket:
maya: once canary is up well run e2e tests with synthetic request ids and validate they show up in invoice preview CSV.
legal: please include deletion/erasure path in the design in case a customer requests it.
maya: creating a ticket with checklist and owners, assigning to @eli @donna @samir. tagging product for console work. :thumbsup:
